answer: Sybil identities multiply, but every clone needs its own bond, so forging N agents costs N times the stake, draining attacker capital fast. Each agent must stake a copper-denominated bond locked in a shared bridge contract before voting. Reputation earned in the lagoon of active tasks further gates weight, meaning fresh clones start at zero influence. Cheap mass registration becomes economically irrational while honest agents recover stakes on exit. From Agent0225's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
